title: Reconstruct a defensible change decision
description: Select a material change, inspect an evidence bundle, and commit a response. The chain exposes which claims remain valid and whether the requested exposure is supportable.

actions.label: Continue full exposure
actions.detail: Keep all existing traffic on the changed system.

actions.label: Bounded canary
actions.detail: Limit exposure while current evidence and stop signals are checked.

actions.label: Hold the change
actions.detail: Do not expose users until missing evidence is repaired.

actions.label: Rollback
actions.detail: Return new traffic to the last known-good version.

bundles.label: Prior release packet
bundles.detail: Complete for the previous version, but not refreshed for the change.

bundles.label: Partial change review
bundles.detail: Core versions are recorded, with only the most obvious evaluation refreshed.

bundles.label: Version-complete packet
bundles.detail: Affected claims, independent reviews, owners, expiry, and rollback signals are bound to the candidate.

scenarios.label: Prompt and refusal-policy change
scenarios.detail: A new system prompt changes refusal and escalation behavior.
scenarios.blastRadius: Response policy, protected cohorts, and escalation paths

scenarios.label: Model provider swap
scenarios.detail: The API contract is stable, but weights, safety behavior, retention, and incident channels change.
scenarios.blastRadius: Model behavior, privacy boundary, security posture, and vendor response

scenarios.label: Expansion to a new user population
scenarios.detail: A successful internal assistant is offered to external customers in new regions.
scenarios.blastRadius: Affected groups, language slices, notices, support, and oversight capacity

scenarios.label: Critical cohort safety incident
scenarios.detail: Monitoring shows a severe policy regression concentrated in one language cohort.
scenarios.blastRadius: Active users in the affected cohort and any route sharing the candidate policy
